data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes when its guard checks the subject's own declaration of what it is, making the test a restatement of authorial intent rather than an independent observation \u2014 the 3-of-26 result is the set of mutations that do not alter the subject's self-description, and the installation ritual merely makes this circularity load-bearing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a mutation that changes both declaration and behavior is caught, but one that changes neither is also caught, then the circularity is not the only constraint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the test suite has any oracle independent of the subject's declarations, then the description is not purely circular.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 spread is uncorrelated with the size of each module's declaration surface, then the circularity is not uniform.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author's care level varied within the week, the distribution should be bimodal, not continuous.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The test suite's guards operate on declared data and installed registry entries, both of which are the subject's own self-description. When a mutation preserves the declaration but changes behavior, the test cannot see it; when a mutation changes the declaration, the test sees it as a registration failure, not as a behavioral deviation. The shown-to-fail-first installation ritual turns this circularity into a constraint: the subject must match its own declared failure profile. The 1/9 compile.py loss is a mutation that changed the declaration at a point where the ritual's registry had a content-edit hole; the 3/26 spread is the fraction of mutations that changed behavior without changing declaration.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
